items.title: Pug Horton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: if you’re King Oliver or Louis Armstrong or Sidney Bechet

ctx.x: Yes, absolutely. And the same thing applies in other places in England for instance, when people have some frame of reference for what they have seen and they continue to watch and so on. But I think the economics of bringing over musicians is getting harder, and one of the problems that we have, Bobby and I subscribe to as well, is that Bob doesn’t like jam sessions. He really likes a formed group, because as you notice from our recordings, we like musicians that have at least shook hands before they go on the…
you’re Jelly Roll Morton or if you’re King Oliver or Louis Armstrong or Sidney Bechet. But not everybody is, sad to say.
Do you think it sells the music short?
